finalText:
Fixed. Tests 4/4 green.

## Leak

`src/jobs/processOrder.js:9` — release after `await`, no `try/finally`:

```js
const conn = pool.acquire();
const result = await run(conn, order); // rejects for a bad order
pool.release(conn);                    // never runs on reject
```

Bad order rejects, `release` skipped, connection stuck in `inUse` forever. `Pool` has no reaper (`src/db/pool.js:3-5`), so leak permanent.

Request path never leaked — `handlers/api.js` goes through `withConnection`, which has `finally`.

## Logs match

worker.log — failed jobs miss `connection released`, in-use ratchets one per failure, never back down:
```
02:06:15.640 ERROR [worker-1] job order-4122 failed: invalid order payload
02:06:15.645 WARN  [db] pool in-use: 3/5
02:06:20.440 ERROR [worker-1] job order-4123 failed: invalid order payload
02:06:20.445 WARN  [db] pool in-use: 4/5
```
Note `02:06:25.245 WARN [db] pool in-use: 4/5` — order-4124 succeeded, released, stayed 4/5. Only failures ratchet. Then 5/5 at `02:06:30.045`, exhaustion at `02:06:33.000`, worker-1 `FATAL` exit `02:06:35.100`.

app.log lagged behind worker — leak was worker-side, but pool shared, so API starved too: high-utilization climb 2/5 at `02:09:59.200` up to 5/5 at `02:11:14.800`, then sustained `acquire timeout` / `503 (pool exhausted)` until supervisor restarts at `02:13:36.800`. `cron tick: reap-idle-connections ok` lines are misleading — that reaper does not touch this pool.

## Fix

`processOrder` now delegates to `withConnection`, same as request path. Comment updated — it claimed a retry loop needed manual hold, but that loop is gone.

```js
async function processOrder(pool, order, run) {
  return withConnection(pool, (conn) => run(conn, order));
}
```

## Note on test command

`node --test tests/` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on this Node (v22.22.2) — path arg treated as module, not test glob. Not a code bug. Use `node --test` or `node --test tests/pool.test.js`. Both green.

## Worth doing next

Pool has no defense in depth — a future missed release is again permanent. Consider acquire timeout + in-use age reaper, or making `acquire` private so `withConnection` is the only entry point. Say word if you want it.
